statement: Microsoft aims to expand total compute capacity from roughly 12 gigawatts today to more than 38 gigawatts by 2032, with AI-focused infrastructure scaling from about 2 gigawatts to roughly one-third of that total.
why: A tripling of a top hyperscaler's compute footprint sets the multi-year order pipeline for GPUs, facilities and power.

impact.mechanism: Capacity targets of this scale translate into sustained procurement of AI accelerators, datacenter shells, electrical gear and firm power.

evidence.excerpt: Microsoft aims to expand its total compute capacity from roughly 12 gigawatts today to more than 38 gigawatts by 2032 across owned and leased facilities.
AI-focused infrastructure is expected to scale to roughly one-third of the total 38-gigawatt capacity by 2032,

confidence.basis: Secondary republish of Bloomberg reporting, and a Microsoft spokesperson reportedly disputed the projections without offering alternatives.

dispersion: A Microsoft spokesperson reportedly told Bloomberg the capacity projections cited were inaccurate but did not provide alternative figures.
